A RECORD WHOSE REASON COULD BE ANY STRING is a record in which one authority's verdict passes for another's. That is #637 exactly: a PolicyError token reached AuditEvent.reason, and from the record alone nobody could tell which authority had spoken. Removing the string-taking constructors made the containment a property of the TYPE, so there is no producer graph left to discover.

THE LABEL CONJUNCTS ARE THE MIRROR of that. A label that WAS a token would let a reader treat display prose as a machine verdict; two verdicts sharing a sentence would make two different outcomes indistinguishable in the record an investigation reads.

NO authorization_hash_mismatch REASON, because 'mismatch' would report a semantic comparison as Core's when Core only BINDS the artifact — attributing a decision to the layer that binds rather than the one that interprets.

THE TREE-WIDE HALF IS THM-0111's: that exactly two files decide what an mcp-re.* verdict token says is measured there. What is established here is what the audit layer may SAY with them. Not the emission: nothing here establishes a record is written, reaches a sink, or is durable.
